title: SkyDiscover Optimize and Synthesize capability boundary, 2026 main
summary: The current framework separates evaluator-driven Optimize from skill-based system Synthesize. Optimize supports adaptive program search, container evaluators, evaluator artifacts, and AdaEvolve Pareto objectives; Synthesize is described as Codex/Claude-compatible tooling but is not the same as the Optimize CLI search surface.

mechanisms.name: Executable multi-objective algorithm search
mechanisms.description: AdaEvolve adapts exploration across populations and can optimize explicit Pareto objectives while evaluator artifacts feed failure mechanisms into later candidate prompts.
mechanisms.limitations: Search cannot create missing observation information and will exploit evaluator shortcuts if truth, denominators, hard invalidity, or hidden boundaries are weak.

mechanisms.name: Optimize versus Synthesize boundary
mechanisms.description: Optimize evolves a bounded program against an evaluator. The README presents Synthesize as separate test-driven or inductive-deductive skill tooling for multi-file systems; Optimize agentic mode currently exposes read_file and search rather than arbitrary repository mutation.
outputs: Bounded optimized program or separately synthesized system
mechanisms.limitations: Do not claim that the Optimize CLI is a general Codex-style multi-file implementation agent.
